The two predicates are exhaustive and mutually exclusive on both sides, so the 'throws if none match' arm (seam step 26) is unreachable in both.

guards.what: the applier of the chosen curse's power
guards.issue: Narrowed 2026-07-30 (tier-2 campaign): (Task 28.) The APPLIER half is fully fixed: the four knowledge curses now apply their power with applier=ctx.player (knowledge_demon.py:101), matching Disintegration.cs:25-28 / MindRot.cs:25-28 / Sloth.cs:25-28 / WasteAway.cs:28-31's `PowerCmd.Apply(..., base.Owner.Creature, this)` -- load-bearing since PowerCmd.apply's InstancedPerApplier stacking and modify_power_amount gating key off applier identity. STILL OPEN: the card-SOURCE half. PowerCmd.apply (cmds.py) and Power carry no source/card parameter at all -- an architecture-wide absence, not a knowledge-demon defect; it belongs to power_cmd/Power ownership when a listener first reads a power's source. Witness: test/test_monster_tier_families.py::TestKnowledgeDemonCurseApplier.  The text it replaced read: In the game the curse card applies its own power with the PLAYER as applier and the card as the source: Disintegration.cs:25-28, MindRot.cs:25-28, Sloth.cs:25-28 and WasteAway.cs:28-31 all read PowerCmd.Apply<XPower>(..., base.Owner.Creature, amount, base.Owner.Creature, this) - target = owner, applier = owner, cardSource = the card. knowledge_demon.py:84-86 applies it with applier=self, i.e. the Knowledge Demon, and with no card source at all. DORMANT: executed with `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b05.py listeners`, the sim has exactly two modify_power_amount implementers and two on_power_applied implementers outside hooks.py, and none of the four can distinguish these two appliers here - ruined_helmet gates on power_cls is StrengthPower; unsettling_lamp returns early on `target is self.player`, which is true either way; ViciousPower (powers.py:1158-1179) gates on name == 'vulnerable'; the stat-stealer at powers.py:3090-3101 gates on name being its own strength/dexterity id AND a negative delta. Concrete trigger that would make it live: any listener keyed on 'a power the PLAYER applied to themselves' (the game's own Unsettling Lamp shape) or a card-source-aware power hook. Rule 7: leans on sts2_rl/powers.py and the two relic files, unhashed; the four C# card files are in extra_sources.

guards.what: the counter increments AFTER the choice resolves, and guards its own throw
guards.rationale: C# CurseOfKnowledge throws if CurseOfKnowledgeCounter >= 3 (KnowledgeDemon.cs:151-154) and increments at :164, after ChooseCurse has awaited. knowledge_demon.py:87 increments after the apply. The throw is unreachable on both sides because the conditional branch stops routing to CURSE once the counter reaches 3 - and CURSE is only ever entered from that branch or as the initial state.

guards.what: the curse choice is delegated to the agent instead of a UI screen
guards.rationale: C# CardSelectCmd.FromChooseACardScreen (KnowledgeDemon.cs:183) blocks on a human pick and draws no RNG. The sim routes the same two-card choice through CombatState.select_cards('curse_of_knowledge', choices, 1) (knowledge_demon.py:81), which hands it to the installed card_selector - the RL policy or the conformance driver - and only falls back to _rng.sample when no selector is installed (combat.py:575-581). The choice channel is the sim's stand-in for the player, so the observable is the same decision made by the same agent; the no-selector fallback is a default, not a model of the game. Flagged rather than waived because the fallback DOES draw from the shared combat rng where the game draws nothing - which is why the conformance driver installs a selector. Rule 7: leans on sts2_rl/combat.py, unhashed.

guards.rationale: KnowledgeDemon.cs:217 heals 30 * CombatState.Players.Count; in single-player Ironclad scope that is 30, and knowledge_demon.py:99 heals _PONDER_HEAL = 30. The multiplayer scaling is out of scope by the contract's global-scope clause.

PonderMove damages, then heals, then applies Strength (:215-218); knowledge_demon.py:95-100 keeps that order. Sim constants 17/8/3/11/30/2.

KnowledgeDemon.cs:169-172 returns early for a dead target. In Ironclad scope the only target is the player, and a combat in which the player is dead has already ended on both sides, so the guard is inert - it exists for the multiplayer loop at :157-162.
